# Schemas

The records the Store keeps. Part of the [specification](README.md); why the fields are the way they are is in the [Schema decisions](../decisions.md#schema).

## Event

```jsonc
{
  // Generated by the Application before calling Append; the Store only checks
  // that it is unique within the Stream (AppendEvent.05)
  "event_id": "uuid",
  // The target Stream's name, e.g. "Chores"
  "stream_id": "string",
  // Assigned by the Store: one counter per Node that has appended to this
  // Stream, keyed by node id; a Node absent from the map counts as 0
  "vector_clock": { "node-a": 3 },
  // The Event's type, e.g. "TodoFinished"
  "type": "string",
  // Assigned by the Store's clock when the Event is appended
  "created_at": "ISO8601",
  "data": { "todo_id": 1, "status": "completed" },
  "metadata": { "schema_version": "1.7.2" }
}
```

`event_id` and `stream_id` are assigned by the Application; the Store never generates identifiers on the caller's behalf. `vector_clock` and `created_at` are assigned by the Store at append time: they record when and where the Event landed in the Stream.

With one writer per Stream, `vector_clock` holds a single entry, the appending Node's own counter, and acts as a position counter. It starts detecting concurrency once several Nodes can append to one Stream.

`data` and `metadata` are opaque to the Store.

## Stream

_Not yet validated against Stream subscription or Node replication needs._

```jsonc
{
  // Sole identifier, chosen by the Application when it creates the Stream
  "stream_id": "string",
  // A deleted Stream no longer exists
  "status": "open | closed",
  // Assigned by the Store's clock when the Stream is created
  "created_at": "ISO8601",
  // Assigned by the Store's clock by the first close; null while open
  "closed_at": "ISO8601 | null"
}
```

There is no separate generated Stream id. In the Rust API, `status` and `closed_at` are one value, `StreamStatus::Closed { closed_at }`.
